name: TherapyNotes
description: TherapyNotes is a behavioral-health electronic health record and practice-management platform for patient records, scheduling, clinical documentation, billing, insurance claims, payments, telehealth, secure messaging and prescribing.
agentUseSummary: TherapyNotes cannot be connected directly to Relay agents because its current official product and support surfaces do not publish a supported third-party account API, delegated OAuth flow, API-key contract, developer portal or remote MCP service. TherapyNotes instead documents role-bound product access and manual or provider-managed exchange workflows, and explicitly tells users not to share accounts or enter TherapyNotes credentials into another website.

blocked.label: Connect a TherapyNotes account
blocked.description: TherapyNotes does not publish a supported delegated OAuth, API-key or remote MCP connection contract for third-party agent platforms.

blocked.label: Collect TherapyNotes credentials
blocked.description: Relay does not collect practice codes, usernames, passwords, temporary passwords, two-factor codes, session cookies or client-portal credentials.

blocked.label: Use private TherapyNotes interfaces
blocked.description: Relay does not reverse engineer undocumented requests or automate private application traffic handling clinical, patient, financial or prescribing data.

blocked.label: Automate TherapyNotes workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not use a staff seat or browser automation to read or change records, schedules, notes, claims, payments, messages, telehealth sessions or prescriptions.

blocked.label: Automate manual data exchange
blocked.description: Documented spreadsheet/PDF exports, secure file imports, clearinghouse connections and HIE submissions are user- or provider-managed workflows, not a general Relay API authority.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled without a supported TherapyNotes account API, delegated authorization contract or remote MCP service.

runtimeSupport.description: No documented public TherapyNotes account API or remote MCP service is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No documented public TherapyNotes account API or remote MCP service is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: TherapyNotes' current official product and Help Center describe a role-controlled web/mobile EHR spanning patient records, clinical notes, scheduling, claims, payments, telehealth, messaging and prescribing, but publish no developer console, third-party application registration, OAuth or API-key authorization, endpoint/schema reference, scopes, rate limits, webhooks or remote MCP service. Documented exchange paths are manual spreadsheet and PDF exports, secure staff-assisted imports, and product-managed clearinghouse, payment, HIE and portal workflows. TherapyNotes' security guidance requires a unique account for each person, says account sharing violates its terms, and instructs users not to enter their practice code, username or password into another website. A staff seat, shared credential or private browser interface is not a supportable agent integration and would create unsafe authority over highly sensitive behavioral-health data.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request TherapyNotes credentials or show Connect. Reconsider only if TherapyNotes publishes a supported distributable account API, delegated OAuth contract, API-key contract or remote MCP service with exact operations, role and practice binding, healthcare-data terms, BAA/security obligations, auditability and revocation.

evidence.supports: TherapyNotes describes one integrated EHR and practice-management product covering records, clinical documentation, scheduling, billing, payments, portal, telehealth, messaging and prescribing, without presenting a developer integration surface.

The current Help Center exhaustively routes account work through product UI features, roles and selected managed partner workflows and publishes no developer/API category or third-party application registration path.

TherapyNotes requires users not to share accounts and instructs them never to enter their practice code, username or password into another website; it also emphasizes role-based access, audit logs and protection of PHI.
TherapyNotes requires separate user accounts and roles, states credential sharing violates its terms, and relies on individual activity attribution for security and compliance.
TherapyNotes documents user-initiated spreadsheet and PDF exports from product tables rather than a programmatic account API.

The supported import path is a limited spreadsheet sent through TherapyNotes' secure portal for staff processing; it excludes clinical notes, billing history and calendars and warns against emailing PHI.

TherapyNotes' current legal FAQ explains that customer healthcare use is governed by updated privacy terms and an integrated BAA, reinforcing the need for an explicit supported third-party data-processing contract.
